'''Benjamin Franklin Cravatt III''' is a professor in the Department of Chemistry at [[The Scripps Research Institute]] in [[La Jolla, California]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Viegas|first=Jennifer|date=February 2, 2016|title=Profile of Benjamin Cravatt|journal=[[Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]|volume=113|issue=5|pages=1109–11|doi=10.1073/pnas.1525099113|pmc=4747733|pmid=26811454|bibcode=2016PNAS..113.1109V|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Considered a co-inventor of [[activity-based proteomics]] and a substantial contributor to research on the [[endocannabinoid system]], he is a prominent figure in the field of [[chemical biology]].  Cravatt was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2014,<ref name=":0" /> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite press release|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|date=April 29, 2014|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|location=United States|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-29-2014-NAS-Election.html|quote=Cravatt, Benjamin F.; professor and chair, department of chemical physiology, The Scripps Research Institute, La Jolla, Calif.|access-date=December 31, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150818062140/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-29-2014-NAS-Election.html|archive-date=August 18, 2015}}</ref> He is Gilula Chair of Chemical Biology, a Cope Scholar, and a [[Searle Scholar]]. In 2026, he was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]].

== Early life and education ==
His father was a [[dentist]] and his mother a [[dental hygienist]], both of whom instilled in Cravatt an interest in biology as a child.<ref name=":0" />

Ben Cravatt is left handed.

Cravatt entered [[Stanford University]] in 1988, graduating in 1992 with a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in the Biological Sciences and a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in History.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bogyo|first1=Matthew|first2=Benjamin F.|date=February 2007|title=Genomics and proteomics: From genes to function: advances in applications of chemical and systems biology|journal=[[Curr. Opin. Chem. Biol.|Current Opinion in Chemical Biology]]|type=Editorial Overview|volume=11|pages=1–3|doi=10.1016/j.cbpa.2006.12.029|last2=Cravatt}}</ref>  He then received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Macromolecular and Cellular Structure and Chemistry from [[The Scripps Research Institute]] in 1996,<ref name=":0" /> where he worked under the joint supervision of [[Dale L. Boger]] and [[Richard Lerner]].

== Research ==
His early contributions to the [[cannabinoid]] field include identification and characterization of the endocannabinoid-terminating enzyme [[fatty acid amide hydrolase]] (FAAH),<ref name=":0" /> as well as the isolation of the novel soporific compound [[oleamide]] from [[cerebrospinal fluid]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Cravatt|first1=B.F.|last2=Giang|first2=D.K.|last3=Mayfield|first3=S.P.|last4=Boger|first4=D.L.|last5=Lerner|first5=R.A.|date=November 7, 1996|title=Molecular characterization of an enzyme that degrades neuromodulatory fatty-acid amides|journal=Nature|volume=384|issue=6604|pages=83–7|doi=10.1038/384083a0|pmid=8900284|bibcode=1996Natur.384...83C|s2cid=4288981}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Cravatt|first1=BF|last2=Prospero-Garcia|first2=O|last3=Siuzdak|first3=G|author-link3=Gary Siuzdak|last4=Gilula|first4=NB|last5=Henriksen|first5=SJ|last6=Boger|first6=DL|last7=Lerner|first7=RA|author-link7=Richard Lerner|date=June 9, 1995|title=Chemical characterization of a family of brain lipids that induce sleep|journal=Science|volume=268|issue=5216|pages=1506–9|doi=10.1126/science.7770779|pmid=7770779|bibcode=1995Sci...268.1506C}}</ref>

Cravatt and colleagues pioneered the [[activity-based protein profiling]] (ABPP) chemical proteomic technology, which they used in 2010 to elucidate certain global proteomic features of cysteine proteases.<ref name=":0" />  Cravatt's lab has since combined the ABPP technology with [[metabolomics]].<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and professional service ==
Among the awards that Cravatt has received are the [[TR100]] Award in 2002, the [[Eli Lilly Award in Biological Chemistry]] in 2004, the [[ASBMB-Merck Award]] in 2014 and the [[Sato Memorial Award]] in 2015.<ref name=":0" />  Cravatt also received an [[NCI MERIT]] grant in 2009.<ref name=":0" /> In 2022 he was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2022/02/08/benjamin-f-cravatt-iii/ |title=Wolf Prize in Chemistry 2022 |access-date=February 9, 2022 |archive-date=March 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331024955/https://wolffund.org.il/2022/02/08/benjamin-f-cravatt-iii/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Cravatt is a co-founder of Vividion Therapeutics, [[Abide Therapeutics]] and [[ActivX Biosciences]].<ref name="b761">{{cite web | title=Benjamin Cravatt | website=@broadinstitute | date=May 14, 2025 | url=https://www.broadinstitute.org/bios/benjamin-cravatt | access-date=April 16, 2026}}</ref> He formerly served as an Associate Editor for the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'' and [[Chemical Science (journal)|''Chemical Science'']].<ref name="t515">{{cite web | title=Benjamin F. Cravatt Iii, Chair, Professor | website=eMedEvents | date=May 30, 2025 | url=https://www.emedevents.com/speaker-profile/benjamin-f-cravatt-iii-2 | access-date=April 16, 2026}}</ref>
